title: Deleting a todo has no confirm dialog and no undo
steps: On /today, tap the delete (X) button on a todo. Double-tap it rapidly to also check for a double-click race.
expected: Either a confirm step before an irreversible delete, or an undo affordance after (consistent with Mind's Reading/Study/Skills delete paths, which all use ConfirmDialog).
actual: The row is deleted immediately and permanently with a single tap, no confirm dialog, no toast-with-undo. Rapid double-click did not create a duplicate-delete error (deleteMutation is idempotent enough not to crash), but the missing confirm/undo is real and inconsistent with the rest of the app.
evidence: areas/today/scripts/r1-01.mjs console output: rowsBefore=1 rowsAfter=0 clickErrors=0
suspectFile: src/components/dashboard/TodayActions.jsx:91-97 (deleteMutation, no onError, no confirm/undo UI) vs. Mind's ConfirmDialog usage on its delete paths
why: Re-ran r1-01: one tap on the X deletes the row (rowsBefore=1, rowsAfter=0) with no confirm and no undo. The X is a 44px target right beside the todo text, so a sweaty-thumb mis-tap permanently loses the entry, and todos have no history view to recover it from. Same class as fuel-r1-06 (food delete), which was confirmed and fixed with an Undo toast (58cb69a9). deleteMutation also has no onError, so a failed delete is silent.
fixHint: src/components/dashboard/TodayActions.jsx:93-99 - in deleteMutation keep the deleted row (pass the todo, not just its id) and onSuccess show toast('Task deleted', { action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: re-insert {created_by,date,text,domain,source,completed} } }) as in fuel's 58cb69a9; add onError: toast.error('Failed to delete').

title: Two tabs racing the AI-seed insert (code-level risk, not reproduced live)
steps: With an un-seeded daily brief for a given date, open the same /today in two tabs sharing one browser session/localStorage, navigate both to /today simultaneously (racing the mount-time seed effect).
expected: Exactly one todo row per brief action is seeded, regardless of how many tabs mount concurrently.
actual: This run did not reproduce a duplicate: rows=2, exactly 1 row per action, no duplicates. The seed guard (localStorage.getItem(seedKey) checked synchronously, but localStorage.setItem(seedKey,'1') only set inside the insert's async .then()) has a real race window by code inspection, but it is narrow/timing-dependent and was not triggered under this run's network latency.
evidence: areas/today/scripts/r1-02.mjs console output: rows=2 countByText={"OVN-today-r1-02 action A":1,"OVN-today-r1-02 action B":1} pageErrors=0
suspectFile: src/components/dashboard/TodayActions.jsx:56-77 (seed useEffect: sync localStorage.getItem guard vs. async .then() setItem)
why: The attacker reported no bug (severity none): two tabs racing the seed produced exactly one row per action. The race window exists by inspection, but see today-r1-03: the real duplicate source is that the seed guard is per-device localStorage.

title: Client-side de-dupe-by-text hides a legitimate second todo and mis-scopes its toggle
steps: Insert two DB todos rows for the same date with identical text but different domain (e.g. training vs nutrition, both source=ai_generated). Load /today and toggle the one visible row.
expected: Either both rows render distinctly, or if intentionally merged, toggling the visible one has a well-defined, non-surprising effect on the underlying data.
actual: Only 1 of 2 DB rows rendered (dbRows=2, visibleCount=1). Toggling the visible todo only updated 1 underlying row (training) — the other (nutrition) stayed untouched and permanently hidden behind the first.
evidence: areas/today/scripts/r1-03.mjs console output: dbRows=2 visibleCount=1 completedRows=training
suspectFile: src/components/dashboard/TodayActions.jsx:47-52 (de-dupe Set keyed purely on t.text, drops legitimate same-text rows)
why: Re-ran r1-03 (dbRows=2, visible=1, toggle hits only the earliest row). The attacker's setup (same text, different domain) can't be produced by the app, because nothing in src sets todos.domain. So I added r1-03v, which uses a path the app can reach: add the same text twice through the UI (manual). Result: dbRows=2, visible=1, and the counter stays 0/1. The second add saves but never appears, so to the athlete the Add did nothing. The de-dupe is on purpose. Commit ca0997ab ('Fix ToDos') added it together with seedingRef as a band-aid for duplicate AI seeding. The seed guard is localStorage keyed per device, so the phone PWA, Safari and desktop each re-insert the same brief actions for the same date. It also hides double-Enter duplicates, because the Enter handler at :202 skips the isPending guard the Add button has. Removing the de-dupe would expose those real duplicate rows. The proper fix (check existing ai_generated rows before seeding, or a unique (created_by,date,text) index, which is a hosted migration) is a design call.
fixHint: src/components/dashboard/TodayActions.jsx:47-53 - minimal: de-dupe only source==='ai_generated' rows (never hide manual rows), and in the seed effect (:56-78) first select existing ai_generated texts for (user,date) and insert only the missing ones; optional unique index (created_by,date,text) as a proposal migration.

title: Deleting a todo hidden behind a same-text duplicate gives zero visible feedback
steps: With two same-text duplicate todos in the DB (as in today-r1-03), delete the visible (earlier) one.
expected: Some visible feedback that a delete happened (the row disappears, even briefly, or the remaining state clearly differs).
actual: dbRowsAfter=1 confirms the correct underlying row was deleted, but the same-text duplicate (still in the DB) is re-rendered in its place instantly via the de-dupe recompute, so the visible row never disappears at all, before or after reload. The athlete sees no evidence a delete occurred, and the deleted row was silently a different underlying record than what's now shown.
evidence: areas/today/scripts/r1-04.mjs console output: dbRowsBefore=2 dbRowsAfter=1 visibleBeforeReload=1 visibleAfterReload=1
suspectFile: src/components/dashboard/TodayActions.jsx:47-52 (de-dupe recomputed every render, masks the delete) combined with :91-97 (no confirm/undo, see today-r1-01)
why: Re-ran r1-04: dbRowsBefore=2, dbRowsAfter=1, but the visible row never disappears, because the hidden same-text twin takes its place when the list is de-duped again. The delete does happen, but it looks like it failed. Same root cause as today-r1-03, and it happens for real whenever the brief was seeded on two devices: every AI todo then has to be deleted twice. Kept separate from r1-03 because a delete-side fix is needed even if the de-dupe stays for AI rows.
fixHint: src/components/dashboard/TodayActions.jsx:93-99 and :185 - while text de-dupe exists, make delete (and toggle at :169) act on every raw row with the same text for that date (.in('id', ids)) rather than only the earliest id.

title: Todo added right after local midnight silently saves under yesterday's date
steps: Load /today at 23:56 local on day D (no reload since). Advance the clock to 00:08 local on day D+1 with no navigation. Add a todo.
expected: Once local time crosses midnight, the todo is either saved under the new day, or the UI clearly shows it's still logging to the prior day before saving.
actual: The todo was saved with date=2025-09-29 (the stale prior day) instead of the expected 2025-09-30, with zero on-screen indication anything was off. It will not appear when the athlete reopens the app expecting a clean list the next morning.
evidence: areas/today/scripts/r1-05.mjs console output: rows=1 date=2025-09-29 expected=2025-09-30 problems=0
suspectFile: src/pages/Today.jsx:55 (const today = getTodayString(profile?.timezone) computed once per mount, not re-derived from a live clock; passed to TodayActions as a static prop)
why: Re-ran r1-05: saved date=2025-09-29 after the clock crossed to 2025-09-30 00:08. I also added r1-05v, which fires visibilitychange (hidden then visible) plus window focus and waits 5s for refetches, like an iOS home-screen app resumed the next morning. It still saves under 2025-09-29, so nothing re-derives the date on resume. Today.jsx:55 recomputes `today` on each render, but after midnight nothing re-renders the page (clicking + only re-renders TodayActions, which reads the stale `today` prop). Unlike fuel (misattribution to a day you can navigate back to), todos have no date picker or history view, so a todo saved under yesterday is effectively invisible from the next render on. Severity data-loss stands. The fuel approach (5331532b) fits, simplified: /today always means today, so the wasOnToday gate isn't needed. Only the event wiring (visibilitychange, focus, 60s interval) plus a re-render is needed. The query keys and the seed key follow `today` automatically. (r1-05v also logged 5 WebKit 'access control' page errors for queries with date=1969-12-31 right after the synthetic events. This looks like an artifact of Playwright's fake clock plus the synthetic focus refetch, not the app, and it is out of scope here.)
fixHint: src/pages/Today.jsx:55 - add a small useNowDay(tz) hook (useState(getTodayString(tz)) updated on visibilitychange-visible, window focus and a 60s setInterval, same wiring as FoodTracker 5331532b) and use it for `today`; belt-and-braces, recompute getTodayString(tz) inside TodayActions addMutation (:106).

title: No max-length guard on todo text — long input overflows the row with no truncation
steps: Add a todo with ~5000 characters of text.
expected: Either a max-length guard on input, or truncation/line-clamp at render so an extreme-length row doesn't break layout.
actual: A 4996-char todo was accepted and saved in full (todos.text is unbounded TEXT, no client-side max-length). The row rendered with no truncation/line-clamp, causing horizontal page overflow (rowHeight=54px, overflow=true).
evidence: areas/today/scripts/r1-06.mjs console output: rows=1 savedLen=4996 overflow=true rowHeight=54
suspectFile: src/components/dashboard/TodayActions.jsx:99-115 (addMutation, no max-length guard) and :196-199 (row render, no truncation/line-clamp)
why: Re-ran r1-06: overflow=true. The trigger is narrower than the title says. The test string is one 4980-char unbroken token ('x' repeated). Long prose would wrap, and an unbounded TEXT column with no max length is not a bug in itself. The real defect is the row span at :178, which is `flex-1` with no `min-w-0` or overflow-wrap. Any long unbroken token (a pasted URL, the realistic case) pushes the whole /today page wider than the viewport on the phone. Minor layout break, not a restyle.
fixHint: src/components/dashboard/TodayActions.jsx:178 - add `min-w-0 [overflow-wrap:anywhere]` to the todo text span's className (optionally maxLength={500} on the Input at :197).

steps: Toggle a todo's completed state on /today.
expected: The todo's completed state flips and persists.
actual: ok — completedBefore=false completedAfter=true, no console/page errors.

title: Reload mid-flight during add-todo silently loses the entry
steps: Start adding a todo, then reload the page while the insert mutation is still in flight (before its onSuccess fires).
expected: Either the insert completes and the todo persists despite the reload, or the athlete is warned before the reload that unsaved work will be lost.
actual: The todo was lost entirely (rows=0 after reload) with no persisted draft and no warning shown before the reload — the athlete has no way to know the add silently failed to save.
suspectFile: src/components/dashboard/TodayActions.jsx:99-115 (addMutation clears newText/closes the panel only in onSuccess; no local draft persistence, no beforeunload warning)
why: Not a real data-loss path. The original repro holds the POST inside the browser for 4s with page.route, so the request never leaves the client before the reload. That is a harness artifact that stretches a sub-second window to 4s. I measured without the route in r1-08v: the POST goes out ~50-140ms after the tap and the response lands at ~390-495ms. A reload at 0/30/150ms after the tap loses the row, but a reload at 300/700/1500ms keeps it (rows=1, visible after reload). The loss window is about 0.2s from tapping Add. A home-screen PWA has no reload button, and backgrounding the app doesn't abort an in-flight fetch that fast. This is the unavoidable cost of killing the page before the request is committed, not a violation of 'entered data is never lost'. A draft store or beforeunload prompt is not worth adding for a one-line todo.

Load /brief-history at 23:59 local, check buckets, advance 3 min past local midnight, reload, check buckets again.

No crash, no console/page errors. The underlying code-level risk is still real but unconfirmed live: BriefHistory.jsx:42 dateGroup() uses new Date() (browser-local 'now'), not profile.timezone, so a real device/profile timezone mismatch (e.g. an athlete traveling with profile.timezone set to home) could disagree with the rest of the app's day-boundary logic (which uses getTodayString(profile.timezone) elsewhere) — not exercisable from a single-timezone test harness.

title: Today hero and Athlete State read engine tables with different date-resolution logic (latent, not live-reproducible for this test account)
steps: 1. Query athlete_state/engine_params/training_prescription for the test athlete. 2. Load /today, read the readiness hero (StatRing). 3. Load /athlete-state, read VDOT / Model Confidence (AdaptiveEnginePanel). 4. Compare code paths: Today.jsx:85-86 passes an explicit `today` (getTodayString(profile?.timezone)) into useTodayPrescription/useAthleteState; AthleteState.jsx:43-44 calls useEngineParams()/useTodayPrescription() with NO date argument, so those hooks default internally to getTodayString() with no timezone, i.e. the browser/device timezone, not profile.timezone.
expected: Both pages should resolve 'today' the same way so they never silently disagree on which day's engine row is shown.
actual: Confirmed by code inspection: AthleteState.jsx never passes a date into useEngineParams()/useTodayPrescription(), so it resolves 'today' via the browser's local timezone while Today.jsx resolves it via profile.timezone. For this test athlete profile.timezone is null, so both currently collapse to the same value and the pages agree live (verified: hero shows 68, AthleteState VDOT shows 52.1, no console/HTTP errors). The divergence would only surface for an athlete whose profile.timezone is set and differs from their device's timezone (e.g. traveling) — Today would show one day's readiness while Athlete State shows a different day's engine internals with no indication they disagree.
evidence: ui-audit/overnight/shots/r1-09-athlete-state.png; console log: 'DB athlete_state.date=2026-07-01 ... Today hero readiness text="68" | AthleteState ... VDOT="52.1"'; 0 console/HTTP problems
suspectFile: src/pages/AthleteState.jsx:43-44 (useEngineParams()/useTodayPrescription() called with no date arg, unlike src/pages/Today.jsx:85-86)
why: Code confirmed: AthleteState.jsx:43-44 call useEngineParams() and useTodayPrescription() with no date, so they fall back to getTodayString() (device tz). Today.jsx:85-86 passes getTodayString(profile.timezone). There is a real path to the bad state. Profile saves timezone from the device by default (Profile.jsx:147/183), so the live athlete has America/Denver. When he travels east (a persona case), then between local midnight and 00:00 Denver (e.g. 00:00-02:00 ET), AthleteState asks for a training_prescription dated tomorrow in Denver terms. That row doesn't exist yet, so Model Confidence and Interference show '—' while Today shows the current prescription. Not reproducible for the test athlete, whose profile.timezone is null. Minor: a diagnostic page, a 1-2h window, and no data change.
fixHint: src/pages/AthleteState.jsx:43-44 - read profile via useProfile() and pass getTodayString(profile?.timezone) into useEngineParams/useTodayPrescription (same for the bare getTodayString() at :825).

title: Mind Skills: rapid-tap level dots settle correctly under normal network; updateLevel still has no onError/isPending guard for the failure case
steps: 1. Create a tagged skill at level 3. 2. Fire 5 near-concurrent updateLevel.mutate calls in the order 1,5,2,4,3 (Mind.jsx:598-605 dot buttons, mutation at :539-545).
expected: Skill settles on the last-tapped level (3) with no error and no stale flicker.
actual: Reproduced clean on a stable connection: final DB level = 3, 0 console/pageerror problems, single skills row. First attempt hit a transient Supabase auth 429 (shared test-account rate limit from concurrent overnight agents, unrelated to this code path) and was re-run per the runbook's flaky-result rule, then passed cleanly. Confirmed by code inspection that the underlying gap from the case's hypothesis is still real: updateLevel (Mind.jsx:539-545) has no onError handler (contrast the `practiced` mutation right above it at :530-536, which does) and the dot buttons (:598-605) have no isPending disable — so a genuinely failed request among a rapid-tap burst would give zero user feedback and could leave the DB on a level that doesn't match what's shown (not observed live here since all 5 requests succeeded both runs).
evidence: console log: 'PASS today-r1-10 :: finalLevel=3 (expected 3, last tap) rows=1 problems=[]'; ui-audit/overnight/shots/r1-10-after-rapid-taps.png
why: The attacker reported no bug (severity none): rapid level taps settle on the last tap. The missing onError on updateLevel (Mind.jsx:539-545) is only a code-level observation with no failure seen.

title: Mind Skills 'Practiced' while offline: onError never fires — react-query pauses and silently completes the mutation on reconnect with no queued/pending indicator
steps: 1. Create a tagged skill, not yet practiced today. 2. context.setOffline(true). 3. Tap 'Practiced' (Mind.jsx:620, practiced.mutate at :530-536). 4. Wait 4s while still offline, check DB + UI. 5. context.setOffline(false), wait ~2.5s, check DB again.
expected: Per the case's stated risk, a clear 'Failed to update' toast (Mind.jsx:536) should fire while offline and the DB should stay unchanged.
actual: While offline: DB unchanged (correct) and no false optimistic UI (correct), BUT no 'Failed to update' toast fired either — the button just does nothing visible, no toast, no 'queued' state. After reconnecting (~2.5s later), the mutation silently completed and the DB was updated with no confirmation shown to the user. Root cause: react-query's default mutation networkMode ('online') PAUSES a mutation while offline instead of erroring it, then auto-fires it on reconnect. The onError handler at Mind.jsx:536 is effectively dead code for a real offline scenario — it only helps a genuine server-side error, not a connectivity drop, which is the more realistic offline case at a gym. Net effect: no data loss, but a tap at the gym with a spotty signal gives zero feedback for however long the phone stays offline, then completes invisibly later with no confirmation.
why: Re-ran r1-11: while offline, the Practiced tap leaves the DB unchanged, shows no toast and changes nothing on the card. The row updates silently after reconnecting. The default react-query networkMode 'online' pauses the mutation, so onError at Mind.jsx:536 never fires for a dropped connection. No data is lost, but the tap gives zero feedback on a spotty gym signal. This is the pattern fuel fixed in f2590dcd (show an honest 'saves when back online' state). Minor.
fixHint: src/pages/Mind.jsx:620 - when practiced.isPaused && practiced.variables === skill.id, render the button label as 'Offline - saves when back online' (mirror FoodTracker f2590dcd).

title: Coach: reopening a review whose clip is missing from storage leaves the dialog stuck on 'Loading clip…' forever
steps: 1. Insert a tagged form_reviews row with a clip_path that has no matching object in the 'physique' bucket. 2. On /coach, open Past reviews, tap the tagged entry (reopenReview, Coach.jsx:110-115). 3. Observe the dialog.
expected: An error message replaces the loading spinner, or the dialog offers a way to tell the clip is missing.
actual: Confirmed live and reproducible: createSignedUrl returns an HTTP 400 (object not found) — `const { data: s } = await supabase.storage.from('physique').createSignedUrl(...)` destructures only `data` and never checks the `error` field, so `s` is `undefined` on this failure, `s?.signedUrl ?? null` evaluates to `null`, and the dialog is left rendering its 'Loading clip…' spinner permanently (confirmed still stuck after 6s wait). The X close button in the header still works, so the user isn't fully trapped, but there is zero indication anything went wrong — it just looks broken/hung.
evidence: ui-audit/overnight/shots/r1-12-reopen-bogus-clip.png; console: HTTP 400 on storage/v1/object/sign/physique/OVN-today-r1-12/nonexistent.mp4; body text tail ends '...Loading clip… X' at both 3s and 6s
why: Re-ran r1-12: createSignedUrl returns 400, and the dialog is still on 'Loading clip…' at both 3s and 6s. reopenReview (Coach.jsx:110-115) discards `error`, so url=null, which renders the permanent spinner. Besides a clip missing from storage, a more common path is reopening a past review while offline or on a flaky connection: createSignedUrl fails the same way and spins forever. The X still closes the dialog, so the athlete isn't trapped. error-msg.
fixHint: src/pages/Coach.jsx:110-115 - destructure { data: s, error } and on error/no signedUrl set openReview({ review, url: null, error: 'Clip unavailable - check your connection or re-upload' }) and render that text instead of the spinner at :243-247.

title: AthleteState engine-value guards use `!= null`, which is not NaN-safe (latent; no live write path found that actually delivers a raw NaN through JSON)
steps: 1. Read current engine_params/training_prescription for the test athlete (read-only, no mutation — per the case's own fallback instruction, since safely injecting a tagged NaN into a single-row-per-athlete table without corrupting it isn't feasible). 2. Inspect AthleteState.jsx:106 `{vdot != null ? Number(vdot).toFixed(1) : '—'}` and :119 `{confidence != null ? Math.round(confidence * 100) + '%' : '—'}`.
expected: A non-finite engine value should degrade to the em-dash fallback, never render literally as 'NaN%' or 'NaNd'.
actual: Confirmed by inspection: `NaN != null` evaluates to `true` in JS, so if `vdot` or `confidence` were ever a literal NaN, these guards would NOT catch it and would render 'NaN' text. However, investigated the realistic path for this to happen and found real friction: these fields are jsonb, transported as JSON, and JSON has no NaN literal — Postgres' jsonb parser rejects a bare `NaN` token as invalid JSON, so an engine write that tries to persist float('nan') would most likely fail at insert time (a write-time engine error) rather than silently landing as a renderable NaN. The one path that could still produce a client-side NaN is local arithmetic — e.g. AthleteState.jsx:71 `vdotTrend = vdot - vdotHist[...]` when vdot is null and history has ≥2 entries — but that specific case is inadvertently protected: the display gate at :107 (`Math.abs(vdotTrend) >= 0.05`) evaluates to `false` for NaN, so nothing renders. Net: the `!= null` guards on :106/:119 are a real defensive gap worth a one-line fix (`Number.isFinite(...)` instead of `!= null`), but current live data (vdot=52.1, confidence unset/—) shows no NaN and no exploitable write path was found in this pass.
repro: ui-audit/overnight/areas/today/scripts/r1-09.mjs (same read used for the confidence/vdot values; no separate script needed since this is a code-inspection finding)
evidence: code inspection of src/pages/AthleteState.jsx:71,106,107,119; live values observed via r1-09.mjs: VDOT=52.1, Model Confidence unset for today
suspectFile: src/pages/AthleteState.jsx:106,119 (and :71 for the vdotTrend NaN case, which is already inadvertently guarded)
why: Latent, and I found no real path. vdot_state and banister_state are jsonb columns (remote_schema.sql:382-392), and jsonb has no NaN: an engine write of float('nan') fails at insert (or at json.dumps with allow_nan=False) instead of storing a value that could render. The only client-side NaN (vdotTrend at :69 when vdot is null) is already gated by Math.abs(NaN) >= 0.05 being false. Swapping in Number.isFinite would be harmless hardening, but there is no bad state to reach.

title: CSP has no media-src, so Coach clip preview and past-review playback are blocked
steps: Upload a tagged object to physique/<uid>/form/, insert a tagged form_reviews row pointing at it, open /coach > Past reviews, tap it (verify-found, from the r1-13 incidental note).
expected: The signed-URL clip plays in the review dialog, and a newly chosen clip previews before upload.
actual: WebKit logs 'Refused to load https://<project>.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/sign/physique/...' for the reopened review's <video>. r1-13 saw the same for the blob: preview URL. index.html:40 CSP sets default-src 'self' and no media-src, so both the pre-upload preview (blob:) and every past-review clip (https://*.supabase.co) are blocked. There is no public/_headers override, so production has the same CSP.
evidence: r1-13v console: cspBlocks=["Refused to load https://fizdftijlbcnjmemrvao.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/sign/physique/.../OVN-today-r1-13v.mp4?token=..."]; r1-13 REPORT CSP error for blob: preview
why: Found during verify and reproduced live with a tagged object and review row (both cleaned up). The only <video> elements that load from a URL are in Coach.jsx (:159 blob preview, :244 signed URL). The camera and barcode views use srcObject, which media-src doesn't govern. So reviewing your own form clip, the core of /coach, can't play the video on the phone.
fixHint: index.html:40 - add `media-src 'self' blob: https://*.supabase.co;` to the CSP meta.
